content_voiceover: This NCCN table maps out systemic therapy for primary CNS lymphoma across three phases. For induction, the preferred backbone is high dose methotrexate at eight grams per meter squared combined with rituximab, often paired with leucovorin and temozolomide, or in the MPV regimen with procarbazine and vincristine. A lower dose methotrexate option exists too, usually paired with consideration of whole brain radiotherapy. MATRIX, which adds cytarabine and thiotepa to methotrexate and rituximab, is another recommended option. For consolidation, the preferred approach is high dose therapy with autologous stem cell rescue, using conditioning regimens like cytarabine and thiotepa followed by carmustine and thiotepa, or the TBC regimen. Alternatives include etoposide with high dose cytarabine, or monthly maintenance methotrexate-based therapy, or temozolomide alone. For relapsed or refractory disease, options are broad: retreatment with methotrexate-based regimens, ibrutinib combinations, temozolomide, rituximab, pemetrexed, lenalidomide, pomalidomide, and even CAR T-cell therapy with tisagenlecleucel as a category 2B option. Notably, a phase one-two study of the BTK inhibitor tirabrutinib in relapsed refractory PCNSL showed an overall response rate of sixty-three point six percent, with a duration of response of nine point two months and progression free survival of two point nine months.
keypoints: Induction: HD-methotrexate 8g/m2 + rituximab, ± temozolomide or MPV/MT combinations
Consolidation: high dose therapy with autologous stem cell rescue preferred
Alternative consolidation: EA, high dose cytarabine, or maintenance methotrexate/rituximab
Relapsed/refractory: ibrutinib combos, temozolomide, lenalidomide, tisagenlecleucel (CAR-T)
Tirabrutinib trial: ORR 63.6%, DOR 9.2 months, PFS 2.9 months
keypoint_voiceover: For PCNSL, induction centers on high dose methotrexate plus rituximab. Consolidation preferentially uses autologous stem cell transplant, with chemo-only or maintenance as alternatives. For relapse, think BTK inhibitors like ibrutinib, temozolomide, lenalidomide, and CAR T-cell therapy. And remember the tirabrutinib data, response rate about sixty-four percent, but short duration of response.
